findings.claim: The OCR Cambridge National in Creative iMedia is a vocational qualification...
findings.truth: The exam board must never be named in student-facing prose. The qualification name alone is enough.
findings.evidence: house rule (checker brief); same pattern in lessons 2, 4 and 5

findings.claim: Creative iMedia J834 has one exam unit (R093) worth 40% of the qualification
findings.truth: The 40% and the one-exam-unit structure are right (spec 4.1.5 PO weightings; spec 2.2). The spec code J834 is a banned string under the copyright-distancing rule and must go.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 qualification structure; spec 4.1.5; checker brief banned-string list

findings.claim: Card 4: q 'Name a key concept from Introduction to Creative iMedia.' / a 'media industry'
findings.truth: Filler card whose answer duplicates card 1. Two flashcards in one lesson must not share an answer. Replaced with a command-word card.
findings.evidence: validator limit (checker brief)

findings.claim: Mark scheme credits 'new media ... emerged more recently / in the last decade or so'
findings.truth: New media sectors are far older than a decade: the internet and computer games both date from the 20th century. The mark scheme awarded a mark for a false date claim.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 1.1 lists the new media sectors and makes no date claim

findings.claim: The OCR specification divides the media industry into two broad categories
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing prose.
findings.evidence: house rule (checker brief)

findings.claim: Card 4: q '_____ Media Sectors Traditional media refers to non-digital media channels that have been around for decades' / a 'Traditional'
findings.truth: An auto-generated cloze card. The answer word 'Traditional' sits in its own question, so the card teaches nothing. Replaced with a convergence card.
findings.evidence: raw card text; checker brief flashcard rules

findings.claim: Card 5: q 'New _____ Sectors New media refers to digital media channels that have arrived more recently and are still evolving' / a 'Media'
findings.truth: Same auto-generated fault. The answer word 'Media' sits in its own question. Replaced with a digital publishing card.
findings.evidence: raw card text; checker brief flashcard rules

findings.claim: 'There are several types of animation you should know: traditional/cel animation, 2D, 3D, motion graphics, stop motion' plus practice question 'Identify one type of animation.' with an exam-style mark scheme
findings.truth: Types of animation are taught in the optional animation NEA unit (R096 topic 1.1: stop motion/claymation, time-lapse, motion capture, CGI, cel, cut out, flipbook), not in the exam unit. The exam unit lists animation only as one of 13 product types, so a direct exam question on animation types cannot be set. The types are kept as background and the practice question is rebuilt from the exam unit's own product list.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 1.1 (product list) and 4.1.2 ('a direct question may be asked about any content in the teaching content column'); spec 4.5 R096 topic 1.1

findings.claim: Card 2: q 'A traditional form of animation where each frame is drawn by hand on transparent sheets called cels.' / a 'traditional/cel animation'
findings.truth: Every word of the answer appears in the question, so the card gives itself away. Question rewritten.
findings.evidence: raw card text; checker brief flashcard rules

findings.claim: The OCR specification organises these into three categories
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing prose.
findings.evidence: house rule (checker brief)

findings.claim: 'There are four production phases: pre-production, production, post-production, and distribution' - repeated in the term definition, the glossary, a flashcard, the conclusion and a knowledge check ('The four production phases are ... and _____', keyed to distribution)
findings.truth: The spec names three production phases. Work planning lists phases as pre-production, production and post-production, and the job-roles content says roles are specific to 'pre-production, production or post-production phases'. Distribution is a separate topic area (topic area 4), not a production phase. The knowledge check therefore marked a wrong answer as right.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 3.1 (components of workplans: phases); spec 4.2 topic 1.2 breadth and depth; spec 4.2 topic area 4

findings.claim: Card 4: q 'Name a key concept from Job Roles in the Media Industry (Part 1).' / a 'production phases'
findings.truth: Filler card whose answer duplicates card 1. Replaced with a copywriter card.
findings.evidence: validator limit (checker brief)

findings.claim: The OCR specification identifies five senior roles you must know.
findings.truth: Board named in student-facing prose. The count of five senior roles is correct (campaign manager, creative director, director, editor, production manager).
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 1.2 senior roles list; house rule (checker brief)

findings.claim: 'The specification identifies several transferable skills that Creative iMedia develops: creative thinking and innovation, analytical and critical thinking, digital presentation skills, project planning and time management, problem solving, and teamwork.'
findings.truth: The spec names five transferable skills: problem solving, analytical skills, digital presentation, planning and creative thinking. Teamwork is not one of them; the word does not appear anywhere in the spec.
findings.evidence: spec 5.3 Transferable skills; full-text search for 'teamwork' returns nothing

findings.claim: 'In pre-production ... In production ... In post-production ... In distribution, the finished product is converted into appropriate formats'
findings.truth: The parallel wording sets distribution out as a fourth production phase. Reworded so distribution follows the three phases.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 3.1; see F11

findings.claim: Card 5: q 'Name a key concept from Job Roles in the Media Industry (Part 2).' / a 'director'
findings.truth: Filler card whose answer duplicates card 1. Replaced with a production manager card.
findings.evidence: validator limit (checker brief)

findings.claim: Extended-response ladders end 'Lower band (1-2)' in all ten extended-response mark schemes (two per lesson)
findings.truth: The house band vocabulary is Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band. 'Lower band' is off-vocabulary and sits next to 'Lower-mid band' in the same ladder, which is confusing. Renamed to 'Low band' in all ten.
findings.evidence: checker brief band vocabulary

findings.claim: 'Cambridge Technicals in Digital Media and Information Technology (Level 2 or 3)' in the progression paragraph
findings.truth: The progression routes are correct against the spec. But the literal string 'Level 2' is on the generic validator's banned list, and this qualification cannot avoid it: its own grade scale runs from Level 1 Pass to Level 2 Distinction*, and its progression routes are named by level. The band-name ban needs an exemption for vocational subjects, or this unit will fail validation on correct text.
findings.evidence: spec 2.3 progression diagram; spec 5.4 grading scale; checker brief banned-string list

findings.claim: Match check pairs 'Stop motion' with 'Physical objects moved in small increments between photographs'
findings.truth: The statement is true, but stop motion belongs to the optional animation NEA unit rather than this exam unit (see F8). Left as it stands: it is accurate and harmless background, and rebuilding the match item would cost more than it gains.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5 R096 topic 1.1

findings.claim: Indicative content for the 6-mark question: 'Creative and technical roles may be combined (e.g. director also writes the script)'
findings.truth: Director is a senior role in the spec, not a creative or technical one, so the example does not illustrate the point it is attached to. Too small to be worth an edit to indicative content.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2 topic 1.2 role groupings

summary: All five lessons carry fixes. The serious one is lesson 4: 'four production phases' including distribution, repeated in a key fact, a term definition, the glossary, a flashcard and the conclusion, and keyed as the right answer in a knowledge check - the spec names three phases and puts distribution in its own topic area. Lesson 3 taught types of animation from the optional animation NEA unit as exam content, with a matching exam-style practice question. Every lesson named the exam board in prose, five flashcards were auto-generated filler or broken cloze, and lesson 5 credited the spec with a transferable skill (teamwork) it does not list.
